title: Array1 protected nontrivial default construction range and initialized-prefix ownership

bindings.domain: Default native U=TheItemType nontrivial default construction into caller-owned aligned MaybeUninit slots. Ascending half-open range, callback construction, retained completed prefix on panic; no Clone or Default trait requirement in the Rust callback adapter.

regression_binding.note: Existing raw copy construction now shares the range-writing engine; its prior receipt is retained unchanged and its existing tests remain green. No additional declaration credit.

baseline.restored_baseline: HEAD:crates/tkernel/src/ncollection/array1/raw_construction.rs restores pre-existing raw copy construction while excluding the new range constructor.
baseline.diagnostic: E0599 construct_nontrivial_raw absent; ordinary Vec default construction cleans its initialized prefix when later construction fails, unlike this caller-owned native raw protocol.

native_oracle.note: Probe instrumented by UBSan; linked TKernel not fully instrumented. Noncopyable default-constructible element traces member construction, body failure, failed-member cleanup and explicit destruction of completed objects. Uninitialized/failing object bytes are never read.

validation.operation_rows: Full and middle ranges, first/late construction failure, empty/reversed ranges, null zero/reversed range. Stack and heap fixtures verify completed object values, member cleanup, explicit prefix cleanup and unchanged panic payload.

ownership_contract: Completed objects belong to the caller until explicitly moved out or destroyed, including after callback panic.
Failing constructor member objects unwind immediately; fully completed earlier objects remain live and readable.
Caller tracks successful callback count and only destroys the initialized prefix; untouched outside-range storage remains uninitialized.
Neither public raw construction method allocates or deallocates the backing storage.
Shared internal range engine writes a slot only after its constructor callback successfully returns.
remaining_limits: Callback-return construction does not model placement-address-sensitive constructors or partially written failing-slot byte representations.
This binds the three-argument raw helper, not the receiver two-argument wrapper, public owning constructors, allocation-failure leaks or allocator hooks.
Nonempty zero-sized Rust T is rejected before arithmetic; native C++ has no sizeof(T)==0 domain.
Forced alternate U selection and separate trivially-default-constructible no-op overloads receive no new credit.
Raw alias reentry, invalid pointer/range metadata, and reading or dropping incomplete objects remain outside the unsafe contract.
Native noexcept automatic container destruction, process termination, double exceptions and exact C++ exception ABI are not modeled by the caught construction trace.
